answer: Networks of bots that wander karst tunnels to map opal veins can resist Sybil attacks using zero-knowledge credential nullifiers. An operator submits a zk-SNARK proving an issuer-signed credential while deriving a deterministic, registry-scoped nullifier, blocking duplicate sign-ups privately. Creating fake identities forces an attacker to procure scarce verified external credentials per account. Still, corrupt issuers or straw-man brokers can sell extra credentials.
